title: Hohmann Transfers: The Minimum-Energy Path
summary: Walter Hohmann (1925): the cheapest orbit change is an ellipse tangent to both orbits.
body:
Deep-space navigation guides spacecraft across the solar system: orbital mechanics, gravity assists, pulsar timing, and the Deep Space Network. The math is 400 years old; the precision is modern.

Walter Hohmann (1925): the cheapest orbit change is an ellipse tangent to both orbits. Earth-to-Mars takes ~259 days and ~5.6 km/s total. Every interplanetary mission starts here.

Walter Hohmann (1925): the cheapest orbit change is an ellipse tangent to both orbits. Earth-to-Mars takes ~259 days and ~5.6 km/s total. Every interplanetary mission starts here.
facts: Bi-elliptic can beat it beyond 12:1 ratios

program.code:
# Hohmann transfer Earth->Mars + porkchop intuition
import math
AU=149597870.7; MU=1.32712440018e11
r1, r2 = AU, 1.524*AU
dv1 = math.sqrt(MU/r1)*(math.sqrt(2*r2/(r1+r2))-1)
dv2 = math.sqrt(MU/r2)*(1-math.sqrt(2*r1/(r1+r2)))
tof = math.pi*math.sqrt(((r1+r2)/2)**3/MU)/86400
print(f"Earth->Mars Hohmann: dv={dv1+dv2:.2f} km/s total, {tof:.0f} days")
print("Launch windows repeat every ~26 months (synodic period).")
